Hi Angie,

When creating your unmarked frame you can specify y as follows and it should divide it for you based on the occasions you choose. You can try something like this below:

# This will take all the detection/non-detection data for the first 6 occasions
umf1 <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y        = det_hist_sample2[,2:7],
                          siteCovs = site.covs,
                          obsCovs  = obs.covs)

# This will take all the detection/non-detection data for the last 6 occasions
umf2 <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y        = det_hist_sample2[,8:13],
                          siteCovs = …,
                          obsCovs  = …)


Kind Regards,
Philip Faure

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: sub-divide detection history dates in single-season occu model
parts:
If you want to compare detection probability models for the two seasons, then I would argue that you don't want separate analyses.  You want to create a dummy variable (or factor) that identifies the season and use the complete data set.  Otherwise you'd be throwing away information about the status of the site.

I'm assuming that because you want to use occu that the occupancy status must be identical in both seasons.  (Otherwise, if the occupancy status can different in between seasons, then you'd want to use colext.)   So if you perform separate analyses, then at a site where you have detections in one season but not the other, then you'd not be using the information in one of the analyses which would identify the true status of the site.

Here is one way (of many ways) to create an unmarked data frame identifying season and perform the desired analyses. 

# Load library
  library(unmarked)
 
# Get data
  y = read.csv("det_hist_sample2.csv")
 
# Create season 1 and season 2 observation level variables
  nSites = dim(y)[1]
  season1 = matrix(rep(c(1,0), nSites, each=6), nrow=nSites, byrow=TRUE)
  season2 = matrix(rep(c(0,1), nSites, each=6), nrow=nSites, byrow=TRUE)
  x = matrix(runif(12*nSites), nrow=nSites)
  obs.covs = list(season1=season1, season2=season2, x=x)

# Create unmarked data frame
# The first column in y is a row identifier so it is skipped.
  ufo = unmarkedFrameOccu(y=y[,-1], obsCovs=obs.covs)

# Separate detection probabilities for each season
  occu(~-1 + season1 + season2 ~1, ufo)
 
# Same model as above but the P-value for season1 is associated with
# the test of equivalent seasonal detection probabilities.
  occu(~season1 ~1, ufo)
 
# Model with different slopes and intercepts by season for the covariate x
  occu(~season1 + x + season1:x ~1, ufo)
# Same model as above but explicitly obtaining separate estimates for each
# slope and intercept.
  occu(~-1 + season1 + season2 + season1:x + season2:x ~1, ufo)
  
However, with your data set there is (I think) a big problem:  when one season has no detections, the other season has at least one detection.  That occurs for all 28 stations (sites).  That seems very odd.  Is it possible that the data set you were given had surveys in one season but not the other?

Jim

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: sub-divide detection history dates in single-season occu model
parts:
As a statistician it's not that I don't believe you (well, maybe that's it a little) but that in some cases having all detections in one time period and not the other (when it's not consistently the first or second time period with the detections) should cause some concern.  If the per visit detection probability is very low, then that can certainly be the case.  But is it the case here?  The per visit detection probability (ignoring any covariates) is around 0.083.  That is low.  The probability that there is at least one detection in 6 visits is around 0.4.  So the proportion of occupied sites with at least one detection in a 6-visit time period and no detections in the other 6-visit time period is around 0.48.  But your sample data set has 100% with that condition when one would expect around 48% (and the sample data set contains only sites with at least one detection).  (If you're that good at getting extreme results, please buy a lottery ticket for me.)

But my poor attempts at humor aside...If there is some condition where detection is typically found in one time period but not the other, then you'll need to model that.  Maybe that's some change-in-weather covariate unrelated to occupancy. I just don't know.  But some covariate associated with season to explain that phenomenon might be warranted.

About colext:  If occupancy might change between seasons at a site, then occu won't do.  You'll need something like colext.  This is the "closure" requirement:  occu models assume that occupancy status does not change at a site during a season.  This is critical for you to choose which analysis to use.  Your statement "The detection/occupancy is expected to differ, however, among sites and it may vary throughout the season." suggests that the closure assumption doesn't hold.

About creating "dummy variable/factor":  Separate analyses won't allow you to properly compare detection models of the two seasons.  Your estimates of the parameters might be just fine but the standard errors will likely be off (and likely too large in this case).  A very rough analogy of performing separate analyses with separate data sets would be having paired measurements but analyzing the difference with a two-sample t-test rather than the more appropriate paired t-test.  Doing so ignores the sampling design as the two time periods are matched on the same site.

About plots:  You might want to ask that question separately because it's kinda buried with all of this other stuff.  Having a fresh question I think would get you more targeted help.

Jim
